status: analytical role-family map for owner review; not a universal promotion ladder
principle: Live production uses branching employer-, venue-, tour-, union-, and department-specific role structures. Layers below describe recurring responsibility patterns, not guaranteed promotions or authority.

common_layers.label: General production support / new hand
common_layers.meaning: Works under assigned direction; learns call flow, communication, handling, organization, and stop/ask boundaries.

common_layers.label: Department support
common_layers.meaning: Provides bounded support inside a department while preserving technician/system ownership.

common_layers.label: Technician / craft worker
common_layers.meaning: Performs department-specific work within demonstrated competence, employer assignment, site rules, and any required qualification.

common_layers.label: Senior / specialist technician
common_layers.meaning: Handles deeper systems, troubleshooting, prep, documentation, or specialist interfaces; title and authority vary widely.

common_layers.label: Lead / head / crew chief
common_layers.meaning: Appointed responsibility for people, workflow, verification, communication, and handoffs; appointment does not create unrelated specialist authority.

common_layers.label: Design / engineering / management / coordination
common_layers.meaning: Role-specific planning or system responsibility such as designer, engineer, production manager, stage manager, technical director, or operations manager.

entry_ecosystem: IATSE local or venue labor pool

branches.name: Staging / Structures
branches.boundary: Structural assembly acceptance, engineered decisions, powered equipment, rigging interfaces, and manufacturer-specific authority remain with trained/authorized personnel.

branches.name: Scenic / Carpentry
branches.boundary: Structural, machinery, powered-tool, automation, and engineered decisions depend on role competence and authorization.

branches.name: Lighting
branches.boundary: Electrical qualification, energized work, system design, focus/programming authority, and specialist commissioning are not implied by beginner support training.

branches.name: Audio
branches.boundary: System tuning, electrical interfaces, RF coordination, network administration, console/system decisions, and specialist commissioning require role competence/authorization.

branches.name: Video / LED
branches.boundary: Structural support, powered access, electrical work, processing/configuration, commissioning, and specialist network work remain bounded.

branches.name: Backline / Props / Wardrobe
branches.boundary: Artist/tour/department ownership controls adjustments, presets, repairs, substitutions, and acceptance.

branches.name: Rigging
technician_families: qualified/competent rigger roles as defined by employer/site/credential context
branches.boundary: No novice procedural rigging, work-at-height, load calculation, point selection, rescue, or structural acceptance. External qualification and site authority control.

branches.name: Production Power / Electrical
branches.boundary: No energized work, tie-in, testing, load-planning authority, or electrical qualification is created by Crew Blueprint.

branches.name: Site Operations
branches.boundary: Emergency command, crowd engineering, structural acceptance, security/medical authority, and specialized equipment remain with responsible organizations.

branches.name: Logistics / Warehouse / Equipment Movement
branches.boundary: Powered industrial equipment, regulated cargo acceptance, driving, and load-plan authority require separate authorization/qualification.

branches.name: Stage Management / Show Flow
branches.boundary: Authority is appointment- and production-specific; online study does not appoint a learner to call or control a show.

branches.name: Production Management / Production Office
branches.boundary: Budget, labor, contract, safety-program, engineering, and final operational authority depend on employer appointment and external professional responsibilities.

career_rules: Do not show L0-L5 as one mandatory ladder.
Workers may move laterally between branches, employers, markets, shops, venues, and tours.
A lead title is an appointment/responsibility relationship, not proof of specialist competence in another trade.
Rigging, electrical/power, structural, automation, powered-equipment, pyro, laser, and work-at-height responsibilities require their own qualification/authorization context.
Current employer, local, vendor, market, and opportunity information should be retrieved from Production Atlas rather than copied into static course claims.
